items.text: The Mythology Of Conscious AI — Overview
A robed alchemist-creator in a workshop, shaping a clay humanlike figure with his hands; beside him a glass vessel holds a small cloned form and a jointed wooden android stands waiting.
items.context: playing God by creating artificial versions of human beings

items.text: PLAYING GOD
A humanoid machine figure with head bowed, an iron collar and slack chain about its neck, faint radiating lines of anguish around it.
items.context: with consciousness comes moral status, the potential for suffering and, perhaps, rights

items.text: MORAL STATUS OF MACHINES
Two thick corded ropes lying side by side, bound tightly together by three thinner cords wrapped around them like knots.
items.context: bundle intelligence and consciousness together can be traced to three baked-in psychological biases

items.text: BINDING THE BUNDLE
Two machines side by side: one a speaking terminal ringed with a faint halo of light; the other a model of a twisting protein ribbon, plain and unhaloed.
items.context: Nobody, as far as I know, has claimed that DeepMind's AlphaFold is conscious

items.text: ALPHAFOLD FEELS NO HALO
A cinnamon bun on a plate with a nun's face visible in its swirled dough, beside a slice of toast bearing a fainter half-formed face.
items.context: seeing patterns in things, like a face in a piece of toast or Mother Teresa in a cinnamon bun

items.text: FACE IN THE BUN
A cross-section of a single neuron shown mid-pulse, expelling small dark particles of waste like a tiny biological bellows.
items.context: some neurons fire spikes of activity apparently to clear waste products created by metabolism

items.text: NEURONS FLUSHING WASTE
A Watt governor atop a steam engine: two weighted balls swinging outward on hinged arms, closing a valve as the engine runs.
items.context: the cognitive scientist Tim van Gelder gave an influential example, in the form of the governor of a steam engine

items.text: THE STEAM ENGINE GOVERNOR
A coffee cup on a table with grey arrows curving inward from a brain-shape toward it, and black arrows curving outward from the cup back toward the brain.
items.context: The conscious experience of a coffee cup is underpinned by the content of the brain's predictions

items.text: THE COFFEE CUP OF PREDICTION
A weather-office building filled with humming mainframes, above which a small comic hailstorm cloud improbably forms indoors.
items.context: a hailstorm is likely to arise inside the computers of the U.K. meteorological office

items.text: HAILSTORM IN THE MAINFRAME
A heavy iron gate standing slightly ajar in a stone archway, a thin blade of light spilling through the gap rather than the gate being shut fast.
items.context: nothing in what I've said rules out the possibility of artificial consciousness altogether

items.text: THE GATE LEFT AJAR
A smith at a forge hammering a humanoid machine into shape, sparks flying while storm clouds and jagged cracks spread across the workshop wall behind him.
items.context: Creating conscious machines would be an ethical disaster.

items.text: FORGING A DISASTER
A glass laboratory vessel holding a small pale brain-like organoid afloat in fluid, faintly glowing, watched warily by a robed scholar, with a plain unremarkable chatbot box set aside.
items.context: the accidental emergence of consciousness in cerebral organoids (brain-like structures typically grown from human embryonic stem cells)

items.text: THE ORGANOID IN THE JAR
A crude carved stone-age figurine lying beside a faint glowing ghost-shaped silhouette, both examined by a seated scholar with a quill.
items.context: the idea of the soul might seem as outmoded as the Stone Age

items.text: THE SOUL AS STONE AGE RELIC
Inside: Why We're Fooled
A wide blue sky over open land, and beside it a steaming coffee cup with visible heat-waves rising from it.
items.context: The blueness of the sky on a clear day. The bitter tang and headrush of your first coffee.

items.text: BLUE SKY, FIRST COFFEE
A telescope shaped like a human silhouette, through which a distant landscape is being viewed, everything seen through its human-formed eyepiece.
items.context: the tendency to see things through the lens of being human

items.text: THE LENS OF BEING HUMAN
A robed hand pouring a glowing golden liquid into a plain mechanical figure, the liquid spreading through it like a dye.
items.context: we naturally imbue them with other qualities we feel are characteristically or even distinctively human

items.text: IMBUING THE MACHINE
A dim bedroom at night with a translucent ghostly figure standing at the foot of a bed, watched by the person lying in it.
items.context: see a dead relative standing at the foot of the bed

items.text: A DEAD RELATIVE AT THE BED
A steep curve drawn rising across a chart, with several tiny identical figures standing at different points along it, each equally astonished.
items.context: on an exponential curve, every point is an inflection point

items.text: EVERY POINT AN INFLECTION
Two figures in a spare room, one gesturing toward a glowing humanoid machine standing between them as if witnessing a birth.
items.context: it's not the history of man, that's the history of Gods

items.text: THE HISTORY OF GODS
The same cinnamon bun with a nun's face in its swirled dough, beside the faintly-faced slice of toast, echoing the overview's closing scene.
items.context: seeing patterns in things, like a face in a piece of toast or Mother Teresa in a cinnamon bun

items.text: FACE IN THE BUN
Inside: The Four Arguments
A plank of wood shown in cross-section, its natural grain lines forming deep, embedded rings, as if the assumption were carved into the wood itself.
items.context: so deeply ingrained that it can be difficult to recognize it as an assumption at all

items.text: INGRAINED ASSUMPTION
A silicon chip half-buried in barren desert sand, dry and cracked, beside a small living green sprout with visible veined tissue.
items.context: compared to the dead sand of silicon

items.text: THE DEAD SAND OF SILICON
A surgeon's hands lifting a small silicon chip toward an open skull diagram, in place of a single organic cell being removed.
items.context: progressively replacing brain parts with silicon equivalents that function in exactly the same way

items.text: SWAPPING NEURON FOR SILICON
An old diagram of a Turing machine's tape and reading head, frozen in place, with an hourglass beside it running endlessly and never emptying.
items.context: Turing himself identified various non-computable functions, such as the famous "halting problem

items.text: THE HALTING PROBLEM
A swirling spiral vortex drawn over an undulating hilled landscape, suggesting a flow that curves and settles rather than stepping discretely.
items.context: the mathematics of continuous, dynamical processes — involving concepts such as attractors, phase spaces and so on

items.text: ATTRACTORS IN THE LANDSCAPE
A sleeping head projecting a translucent phantom scene, held in check by visible thin cords tethering it to a beam of light entering from outside.
items.context: Conscious experience in this light is a kind of controlled hallucination

items.text: A CONTROLLED HALLUCINATION
A glowing heartbeat-line running through a human silhouette's chest, connected by faint arrows to a brain shape making predictions above it.
items.context: the basal feeling of being alive all map neatly onto perceptual predictions

items.text: THE BASAL FEELING OF LIFE
A screen displaying an animated rainstorm, while a real potted plant standing just beside it remains completely dry and untouched.
items.context: A simulation of a rainstorm does not make anything actually wet

items.text: THE SIMULATED RAINSTORM STAYS DRY
A robed scholar standing before a large glass orb that contains a miniature nested world within itself, gesturing toward it.
items.context: the "simulation hypothesis," associated most closely with the philosopher Nick Bostrom

items.text: BOSTROM'S NESTED WORLD
A wagon rolling forward down a road, its bench seat clearly empty of any rider, though the wagon itself moves swiftly onward.
items.context: consciousness is very unlikely to simply come along for the ride as AI gets smarter

items.text: NOT ALONG FOR THE RIDE
